messages.content: 尋找Netflix上《六人行》的電視節目列表及其評分，以及Hulu上《我們的辦公室》和《怪奇物語》的評分，並按照評分排序。

function.name: streaming_services_shows_list_and_ratings
function.description: Get a list of shows and their ratings on specific streaming services. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

streaming_service.description: Name of the streaming service. E.g., Netflix, Hulu, etc.

show_list.description: List of show names to search for on the platform.

sort_by_rating.description: If set to true, returns the list sorted by ratings. Defaults to false.

message.reasoning:
The user wants:

- For Netflix: "Six Feet Under" (the Chinese title "六人行")? Actually "六人行" might refer to "Six Feet Under"? Wait "六人行" could also be "Six Degrees of Separation"? But likely it's "Six Feet Under". They want the list of shows and their ratings on Netflix.

- For Hulu: "Our Office" (maybe "The Office") and "Stranger Things".

They want ratings sorted.

We need to call the function streaming_services_shows_list_and_ratings with appropriate parameters.

First request: Netflix, show_list ["六人行"]? Or maybe "Six Feet Under". The user wrote "《六人行》", which is Chinese title for "Six Feet Under"? Let's confirm: "Six Feet Under" is a TV series about a family-owned funeral home. In Chinese, it is titled "六人行". Yes, that matches. So we should use "Six Feet Under" as the show name.

Second request: Hulu, show_list ["我们的办公室", "怪奇物语"]. These are Chinese titles for "The Office" and "Stranger Things". We can provide English names: "The Office" and "Stranger Things".

But the function expects show names. It might accept Chinese names too. But better to use English names.

Thus we will make two calls:

1) streaming_services_shows_list_and_ratings({"streaming_service":"Netflix","show_list":["Six Feet Under"],"sort_by_rating":true})

2) streaming_services_shows_list_and_ratings({"streaming_service":"Hulu","show_list":["The Office","Stranger Things"],"sort_by_rating":true})

We need to output the results. We'll call the function twice.
